consent.title: Your Privacy on OnShare
consent.message: We use essential local state and non-intrusive advertising to keep OnShare fast and free. No files, texts, or codes are ever stored on our servers.

howItWorks.title: How OnShare Works
howItWorks.subtitle: Reversed OTP verification and direct browser-to-browser WebRTC streaming. No uploads, no cloud storage, no account required.
howItWorks.step1Desc: The receiver taps Receive to generate a unique 6-digit access code valid for 10 minutes.
howItWorks.step2Desc: The receiver shares the code. The sender enters it to approve connection and sends a preview manifest.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Receiver reviews file details and taps Accept. Encrypted data streams browser-to-browser with zero server storage.
howItWorks.arch1Desc: Unlike traditional tools where the sender issues a link that anyone can open if overheard, OnShare reverses the flow: the receiver generates the code, and the sender must explicitly type it in. Even with a code, nothing is sent until the sender approves and the receiver reviews the incoming manifest.
howItWorks.arch2Desc: When multiple files are shared, OnShare packages them on the fly into an uncompressed ZIP archive using streaming chunk reads. The sender's browser never buffers multi-gigabyte archives into RAM, keeping memory flat and constant.
howItWorks.arch3Desc: In Share Text mode, participants edit a shared plain-text document in real time. Changes are merged deterministically using Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) over WebRTC text data channels without central coordination.

aboutPage.title: About OnShare
aboutPage.subtitle: Fast, private, browser-to-browser sharing built for transparency and simplicity.
aboutPage.missionDesc: OnShare was created to eliminate the unnecessary friction and privacy risks of modern file transfer services. Why should your personal files, slides, or photos sit on a company’s cloud servers just to share them with a friend or colleague sitting in the same room? We believe file transfer should be as direct, lightweight, and private as handing someone a physical flash drive.
aboutPage.principle1Desc: Your files never touch our hard drives or databases. Data streams directly between peer browsers over encrypted WebRTC data channels with DTLS security.
aboutPage.principle2Desc: No sign-up forms, no email verifications, and no tracking cookies. Pair instantly using short-lived 6-digit one-time access codes that expire automatically.
aboutPage.principle3Desc: Transfer single files up to 40 GB directly to disk using the Chromium File System Access API without exhausting browser memory.
aboutPage.principle4Desc: Pair with a single receiver using reverse verification, or toggle Broadcast Mode to share files with up to 50 concurrent recipients with one code.
aboutPage.techDesc: OnShare is powered entirely by modern web standards: WebRTC DataChannels for peer-to-peer transport, Yjs CRDTs for collaborative real-time text synchronization, and ephemeral WebSockets for lightweight discovery signaling. We believe in building sustainable web tools funded ethically by non-intrusive display advertising.

termsPage.title: Terms of Use
termsPage.subtitle: Effective date: September 2026 • Acceptable Use & Guidelines
termsPage.p1: By using OnShare, you agree to comply with and be bound by these Terms of Use. If you do not agree to these terms, please discontinue use of the service immediately.
termsPage.p2: OnShare provides temporary browser-to-browser WebRTC data transmission and real-time live text collaboration without server-side file hosting or user accounts. Both sender and receiver must be online simultaneously for data transfer to succeed.
termsPage.p3: You agree not to use OnShare for any unlawful purpose. Strictly prohibited activities include:
termsPage.li1: Transmitting malware, viruses, trojans, ransomware, or malicious scripts.
termsPage.li2: Distributing infringing copyright material or intellectual property without authorization.
termsPage.li3: Sharing harmful, exploitative, threatening, or harassing content.
termsPage.li4: Attempting to brute-force 6-digit access codes or bypass rate limiting mechanisms.
termsPage.p4: OnShare is provided on an "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE" basis without warranties of any kind. Because OnShare does not inspect or store user content, the sender and receiver are solely responsible for verifying the authenticity and safety of files exchanged.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.subtitle: Last updated: October 2026 • Privacy by Architecture
privacyPage.p1: Files, file names and shared text travel directly from one browser to another, encrypted with DTLS. They never reach our servers, so we cannot read, recover or share them with anyone.
privacyPage.p2: Pairing codes, session identifiers and connection details stay in server memory only. Receive codes last up to 10 minutes, broadcast codes 2, 5 or 30 minutes, and everything is deleted when the session ends.
privacyPage.h3: 3. Your IP address is visible to the other person.
privacyPage.p3: Peer-to-peer connections let the people you connect with see your public IP address. If a direct link fails, an encrypted relay forwards your data and cannot read it. We keep only a hashed IP, and only to prevent abuse.
privacyPage.p4: You need no account, email or password to send or receive. Your browser keeps only small items such as your language, theme and consent choices, plus your receive code until the tab closes.
privacyPage.p5: OnShare may display ads from third-party advertising partners to help cover running costs. These partners may use cookies to show and measure ads. Ads sit outside the transfer area and never access your files or text.
privacyPage.p6: You can ask to access, correct or delete personal data we hold, such as form messages, or withdraw consent at any time through the Contact page. OnShare is designed to align with the GDPR and India's DPDP Act.

landing.heroDesc: Transfer files of any size directly between smartphones, tablets, and computers using end-to-end encrypted WebRTC. No registration, no app downloads, and zero intermediate server storage.
landing.howItWorksSubtitle: OnShare replaces slow cloud uploads with direct browser-to-browser channels. Data streams privately between sender and receiver in three simple steps.
landing.step1Desc: Select your files or paste text into OnShare. A secure, short-lived 6-digit access code is generated instantly to initiate peer discovery.
landing.step2Desc: The receiver enters the 6-digit code on their device. A lightweight WebSocket signal brokers an encrypted WebRTC connection directly between both browsers.
landing.step3Desc: Files stream directly over SCTP data channels with 64 KiB framing and batched disk writes, completely bypassing intermediate cloud servers.
landing.comparisonTitle: Why Choose Direct P2P Over Cloud Storage?
landing.comparisonSubtitle: Traditional cloud services require uploading your entire file to their servers before a recipient can download it. OnShare creates a direct, real-time pipe.
landing.comp1Title: Your Data Never Leaves Your Control
landing.comp1Desc: With typical file lockers and email attachments, your personal photos, documents, and recordings are stored on third-party servers, creating data leak risks. OnShare never writes your file data to a server disk or cloud bucket. The moment the transfer finishes, the session terminates.
landing.comp2Desc: In traditional cloud sharing, you must wait 100% of the upload time before sharing a link. With OnShare P2P streaming, the receiver starts downloading the very first byte the moment you click send, cutting total transfer time in half.
landing.comp3Title: Free from Artificial File Size Limits
landing.comp3Desc: Most free cloud transfer services cap transfers at 2 GB unless you subscribe to expensive plans. OnShare uses the browser’s native File System Access API to stream files up to 40 GB directly to disk without running out of device RAM.
landing.comp4Desc: No email registrations, no password managers, and no persistent tracking cookies. Simply open OnShare in any modern browser, share a 6-digit code, and transfer your files immediately.
landing.faqSubtitle: Everything you need to know about OnShare peer-to-peer file sharing and security.
landing.faq1Q: How does OnShare transfer files without cloud storage?
landing.faq1A: OnShare uses WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication), an open web standard supported natively by Chromium, Safari, Firefox, and Edge. When sender and receiver connect via a 6-digit pairing code, the signaling server only exchanges connection metadata (ICE candidates). The actual file bytes stream directly between the two browsers through an encrypted peer-to-peer data channel.
landing.faq2Q: Is there a file size limit on OnShare?
landing.faq2A: OnShare supports transferring files up to 40 GB in Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera) via the native File System Access API, which writes incoming chunks directly to disk instead of holding them in memory. In browsers where direct disk streaming is restricted, downloads fall back safely to in-memory Blob packaging for files up to available device memory.
landing.faq3Q: Are my files encrypted during transfer?
landing.faq3A: Yes. All WebRTC peer connections are mandatory end-to-end encrypted using DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) with AES-GCM 256-bit cryptography. No third party, internet service provider, or signaling node can inspect, intercept, or tamper with your files in transit.
landing.faq4Q: Can I transfer files between a phone and a computer?
landing.faq4A: Yes! OnShare is 100% browser-based and platform agnostic. You can send files between Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, iPadOS, or ChromeOS simply by opening onshare.me on both devices and entering the 6-digit code.
landing.faq5Q: Do I need to keep the browser tab open while transferring?
landing.faq5A: Yes. Because OnShare streams data directly from the sender’s browser to the receiver’s browser in real-time, both devices must keep their browser tabs open until the progress bar reaches 100%. Once completed, you can safely close the tabs.
landing.faq6Q: What happens if multiple files or folders are selected?
landing.faq6A: When you select multiple files, OnShare automatically bundles and streams them as an uncompressed ZIP archive on the fly using fflate. The receiver receives a single organized .zip file with all folder hierarchies preserved.
landing.faq7Q: How does live collaborative text sharing work?
landing.faq7A: Under the Text Live tab, OnShare provides a zero-install real-time scratchpad powered by Yjs Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs). You can share meeting notes, code snippets, links, and passwords directly across devices with live bidirectional character synchronization.
